uncited: It differs from sibling methods like [3D Student's t Distribution Splatting](4352-3d-student-s-t-distribution-splatting.md), [Generalized Exponential Splatting](4684-generalized-exponential-splatting.md), and [2D Gaussian Splatting](6068-2d-gaussian-splatting.md) by explicitly parameterizing the conditioning step rather than deriving it from a joint covariance matrix.
Direct Beta Splatting (dBS) is a variant of dGS that swaps the Gaussian opacity decay for a Beta opacity decay, following the UBS implementation.
It reuses the direct conditional structure ($\mathbf{L}$, $\mathbf{V}_{pq}$, $\mathbf{V}_{qq}$) but derives coupling from bandwidth.
Unlike dGS, which uses a separate learned coupling $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}$ for position, dBS derives the coupling $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_\beta$ from the opacity bandwidth $\boldsymbol{\beta}$.
It is chosen when a Beta kernel is preferred for its specific decay properties, while retaining the computational benefits of direct conditioning.
